transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-30
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park, Marco Ruiz, Samira Holt (Redwood); Priya Shah, Tom Keller, Aisha Conte, Benji Rao (NovusRetail)

Summary:
Short call to go over incident for NovusRetail on 2025-09-26 where fallback amplification caused a long-tail latency regression during a billing batch. Goal: agree next steps for forensics, confirm safe zone (deployment) patterns, and schedule pilot for regression prevention.

Topics:
- Forensic artifacts needed (eviction traces, prefix/KV cache snapshots)
- Root cause hypothesis: prefix-share + KV eviction under bursty traffic + canary rollout gaps
- Deployment SafeZone concept: limited blast radius canary + graceful fallbacks + health gating
- Security & compliance ask list for pilot

Transcript body:
[00:00:08] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got 60 minutes blocked but we'll try to keep this tight. we were reviewing the post-incident notes, um, and wanted to align on two things: forensics artifacts we need, and the safezone pattern for your next rollout.

[00:00:35] Priya Shah: thanks Lena. quick context: we saw a spike on friday where token latency doubled and then long tail errors spiked. our app started failing downstream because of timeouts in the webhook fanout, so big customer impact.

[00:01:05] Marco Ruiz: right, our initial trace shows a cascade where cache evictions introduced repeated hot prefixes. the runtime tried to fallthrough to a cheaper model variant and that sent load back into the hot path. that double-hit pattern is classic fallback amplification.

[00:01:42] Tom Keller: i still think part of it was our KV settings; we had very aggressive TTLs in staging that somehow made it to prod during the last deploy. there may be a retention mismatch between the K V cache and the prefix store.

[00:02:10] Benji Rao: yeah we pushed a config flip last week, meant for performance; it reduced memory but could've made the eviction rate bump.

[00:02:45] Samira Holt: to be explicit, what artifacts do you all need from our side versus what Redwood will extract?

[00:03:02] Lena Park: good q. On Redwood side Marco will pull trimmed kernel logs, batch scheduling traces, and model switch events. from Novus we need full eviction traces from the K V cache, an exported prefix snapshot if possible, and the infra deploy tag for the window. please put timestamps for the 20:12-20:45 UTC window Friday.

[00:03:40] Aisha Conte: eviction traces — is that a raw dump? security wise we need guidance on what PII might be in those dumps.

[00:04:00] Marco Ruiz: they are operational traces, mostly opaque keys and counters. we'll redact any user ids before sharing. but we do need the index mapping so we can correlate with our scheduling timeline. i'll annotate redaction steps in the artifact handoff doc.

[00:04:28] Tom Keller: can you also capture the rollout metadata — which agents were targeted in the canary and what the autoscale thresholds were?

[00:04:50] Marco Ruiz: yes, we'll include the rollout log and the autoscaler logs; those show when nodes came up and the queue lengths.

[00:05:15] Priya Shah: i want to step back to the hypothesis. are we saying this is purely config (ttl/eviction) or also a serving runtime mismatch?

[00:05:30] Lena Park: short answer: both. the runtime exposed a case where fallthrough policies are not gated with adequate circuit breaking for prefix hotness. that plus low TTLs made the cache thrash. so config triggered the runtime to go into a bad steady state.

[00:06:05] Benji Rao: is that something Redwood has seen before? like, is this common across customers?

[00:06:18] Marco Ruiz: we've seen variants. customers with high prefix reuse and low cache retention can hit this pattern when traffic is bursty. the kernel scheduling + model variant switching amplifies it. it's not frequent but it's a known class.

[00:06:45] Aisha Conte: from a security/compliance lens we also need to see the audit trail — who triggered the last config flip. we need that for our internal review.

[00:07:03] Lena Park: sure — we'll include the deploy tags and the cloud audit logs link. note we may provide pointers rather than raw cloud logs for the first pass.

[00:07:28] Tom Keller: playbook idea — can Redwood propose a "SafeZone" deployment pattern? like a tiny subset canary with a fallback that runs in isolation so it doesn't cascade.

[00:07:44] Marco Ruiz: yep, that's exactly our suggestion. SafeZone has a few levers: limit canary qps to N%, isolate KV namespaces for canary so prefix eviction isn't shared, enable a small grace cache to absorb transient evictions, and add a circuit breaker that trips before fallthrough.

[00:08:15] Benji Rao: can we get a template for the safezone with concrete numbers? e.g., qps limit 5%, grace cache size 200MB, circuit breaker threshold 20% token latency increase.

[00:08:34] Lena Park: we'll share a starting template in the pilot doc; those numbers will be tuned in a dry-run.

[00:08:58] Priya Shah: another ask — we need to know if this will change our cost profile. more caches and isolated namespaces means more memory.

[00:09:12] Marco Ruiz: tradeoff is predictable. we can size a safezone so it adds minimal steady cost; it's primarily a guardrail. Redwood Optimize (transcribed: Redwood Optimizer) will suggest quantization/threading changes to offset memory delta.

[00:09:38] Tom Keller: for the pilot, who runs the dry-run? do you want Redwood SEs to lead or our SREs?

[00:09:48] Samira Holt: we recommend a joint run: Redwood SEs will lead the runbook, Novus SREs operate the staging cluster, and we'll both observe metrics. gives knowledge transfer.

[00:10:06] Lena Park: propose 2-hour dry-run window; first hour baseline traffic replay, second hour flip SafeZone and observe.

[00:10:20] Aisha Conte: what about encryption/KMS — we need to ensure logs/artifacts are stored in your recommended KMS or we can't accept them.

[00:10:32] Marco Ruiz: we support KMS exports and will use your customer-managed key for artifact storage if you prefer. we'll include the handshake in the security annex.

[00:10:50] Priya Shah: let's talk timeline, novus needs this to be in place before the holiday billing window in mid-oct. so we're pushing for pilot by 2025-10-07 and go/no-go by 2025-10-14.

[00:11:12] Lena Park: that's feasible. quick check: are there any procurement/legal blockers?

[00:11:22] Aisha Conte: procurement is engaged. we need the security annex and SOC2 evidence; once those are in we'll be able to greenlight pilot infra access.

[00:11:38] Benji Rao: ok, on the tech side to confirm: what exact logs will Redwood need from our infra agent? we'll need to script that.

[00:11:50] Marco Ruiz: list: eviction trace (time series of evictions per namespace), prefix hits/misses, rollout tag, autoscaler events, kernel scheduling events. i'll send a small script snippet to extract those.

[00:12:18] Tom Keller: please make the script idempotent and note any elevated permissions. we don't want to open up unnecessary IAM perms.

[00:12:35] Marco Ruiz: understoood, script uses read-only monitoring APIs, no elevated compute permissions.

[00:12:50] Priya Shah: any quick wins we can implement now to reduce blast radius while we prepare the pilot?

[00:13:02] Marco Ruiz: yes, two quick wins: bump the KV TTL for high-reuse prefixes, and add a soft circuit-breaker that drops fallthrough attempts when queue length crosses a threshold. both are config flips, low risk, high benefit.

[00:13:26] Tom Keller: we can flip the TTL in staging and promote if stable. i'll schedule that for tomorrow.

[00:13:35] Lena Park: perfect. i'll remind the team that we should also set up additional tracing for the 15-minute windows around the billing job.

[00:13:48] Benji Rao: on the forensics side, how granular will the trimmed kernel logs be? last time the logs were huge and hard to transfer.

[00:14:02] Marco Ruiz: we'll trim to event windows with hashes; we can share an artifact bundle via your S3 with CMK. we'll also provide a short analysis doc with timeline annotations so it's easier to parse.

[00:14:25] Priya Shah: please include a one-page executive summary for our leadership; they want the tl;dr.

[00:14:34] Lena Park: yes, that'll be in the postmortem package.

[00:14:46] Aisha Conte: what about legal — will we need a new addendum for pilot telemetry access?

[00:14:55] Lena Park: we typically use a security annex and an access addendum; i'll route the annex to Aisha and cc procurement.

[00:15:06] Tom Keller: any other mitigations we want to bake into the runtime before pilot? i know you mentioned circuit-breaking, but how about a KV namespace isolation feature?

[00:15:20] Marco Ruiz: we can enable namespace isolation at the routing layer; it's a config toggle on the platform side but requires a small infra tweak to mount separate caches. we can do that for the canary.

[00:15:38] Benji Rao: i like that. it gives us cleaner blast radius.

[00:15:47] Priya Shah: ok let's do a quick readout of responsibilities so we can capture as action items.

[00:16:00] Lena Park: readout: Marco - Redwood forensics bundle and run script; Lena - pricing, pilot template and share annex; Samira - runbook and dry-run facilitation; Tom - provision staging safezone and flip TTL; Aisha - legal/security review. any changes?

[00:16:24] Tom Keller: that matches.

[00:16:30] Aisha Conte: question — will Redwood be proposing a default circuit-breaker implementation or just thresholds?

[00:16:41] Marco Ruiz: we'll propose an implementation using a token-rate threshold plus an exponential backoff on fallthrough attempts; the initial recipe will be opinionated. you can opt to tune it.

[00:17:02] Priya Shah: gentle reminder: please label all artifacts with our internal correlation id NR-20250926 so we can map them to our incident ticket.

[00:17:12] Marco Ruiz: noted, we'll tag everything NR-20250926.

[00:17:25] Benji Rao: are we documenting the safezone runbook in a shared location?

[00:17:32] Lena Park: yes, i'll create a shared doc link and drop a draft of the safezone recipe. Link: https://redwood.ai/safezone/drafts/NR-20250926 (placeholder).

[00:17:50] Tom Keller: regarding metrics — which dashboards should we monitor in real time during the dry-run?

[00:17:58] Marco Ruiz: primary: token latency P50/P90/P99, queue length, eviction rate, model switch count, and downstream error rate. we'll provide a dashboard template.

[00:18:24] Priya Shah: ok that gives us what we need. anything else?

[00:18:30] Samira Holt: just logistics: i'll send calendar invite for the dry-run 2025-10-07 16:00-18:00 UTC and include a pre-read.

[00:18:43] Lena Park: great. last thing — we should pick a small acceptance criteria for go/no-go: P99 token latency increase < 25% vs baseline and no more than 5% fallthrough amplification during the dry-run window.

[00:19:05] Tom Keller: sounds reasonable. we'll prepare load replay to match production pattern as close as possible.

[00:19:18] Priya Shah: on cost again, are there any one-off fees for Redwood SEs to run the pilot? procurement will ask.

[00:19:29] Lena Park: for a single 2-hour pilot we usually include it as part of the support engagement; any extra extended bench hours will be agreed up front. i'll capture that in the pilot doc.

[00:19:45] Aisha Conte: please also include data retention for artifacts — we want them deleted after 90 days unless we request otherwise.

[00:19:57] Marco Ruiz: we'll add a retention clause of 90 days in the annex by default.

[00:20:06] Benji Rao: ok i think that's the core of it. when can we expect the forensics bundle?

[00:20:13] Marco Ruiz: aim to deliver by 2025-10-03, with an annotated timeline doc.

[00:20:22] Priya Shah: great. thanks everyone.

[00:20:30] Lena Park: thanks, we'll follow up with the artifact checklist and calendar invites. meeting adjourned.

[00:21:00] (recording note: truncated transcription; rest of meeting was procedural scheduling and link exchange)

Post-call notes:
- Redwood will redact and tag all artifacts NR-20250926 and upload to Novus S3 with CMK per Aisha's request.
- Pilot scheduled: 2025-10-07 16:00-18:00 UTC (dry-run).
- Acceptance criteria: P99 token latency < 25% increase, fallthrough amplification < 5% during run.
- Links shared: security annex (placeholder), safezone draft doc (placeholder), pilot pricing spreadsheet (will be shared by 2025-10-01).

References (mentioned during call):
